questions.stem: Two runners A and B start simultaneously from the same point on a circular track of \(400\) m. A runs at \(8\) m/s and B runs at \(12\) m/s in the same direction. After how much time will they meet for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
When two runners move in same direction, they meet when faster runner covers one extra lap.
Relative speed = \(12 - 8 = 4\) m/s
Time to meet = Track length / Relative speed = \(400/4 = 100\) seconds

questions.stem: On a circular track of \(300\) m, two athletes P and Q start from the same point and run in opposite directions at speeds \(6\) m/s and \(9\) m/s respectively. When will they meet for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
When two runners move in opposite directions, relative speed = sum of speeds
Relative speed = \(6 + 9 = 15\) m/s
Time to meet = \(300/15 = 20\) seconds

questions.stem: A circular track is \(600\) m long. Two runners start from the same point at the same time. One runs at \(10\) m/s and the other at \(15\) m/s in the same direction. After how many seconds will they meet at the starting point for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first runner to complete one lap = \(600/10 = 60\) seconds
Time for second runner to complete one lap = \(600/15 = 40\) seconds
They meet at starting point after LCM of \(60\) and \(40\) = \(120\) seconds

questions.stem: Two friends run around a circular park of circumference \(400\) m. If they start together and run in the same direction at \(5\) m/s and \(7\) m/s, how many times will the faster runner lap the slower one in \(20\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(7 - 5 = 2\) m/s
Time for one lap by faster runner = \(400/2 = 200\) seconds
In \(20\) minutes = \(1200\) seconds
Number of times faster laps slower = \(1200/200 = 6\) times

questions.stem: On a \(800\) m circular track, A runs at \(12\) m/s and B runs at \(8\) m/s in the same direction. If they start together, when will A be exactly one complete lap ahead of B?
questions.keySolution:
For A to be one complete lap ahead, A must cover \(800\) m more than B
Relative speed = \(12 - 8 = 4\) m/s
Time required = \(800/4 = 200\) seconds

questions.stem: Two cars move around a circular track of \(1200\) m in opposite directions at \(20\) m/s and \(30\) m/s. How many times will they cross each other in \(10\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(20 + 30 = 50\) m/s
Time for one meeting = \(1200/50 = 24\) seconds
In \(10\) minutes = \(600\) seconds
Number of meetings = \(600/24 = 25\) times

questions.stem: A and B start running from the same point on a circular track of \(500\) m. A runs at \(10\) m/s and B at \(6\) m/s in the same direction. What is the distance covered by A when they meet for the second time?
questions.keySolution:
They meet every \(500/(10-6) = 125\) seconds
For second meeting, time = \(2 \times 125 = 250\) seconds
Distance covered by A = \(10 \times 250 = 2500\) m

questions.stem: On a \(600\) m track, two runners with speeds in ratio \(3:4\) start together in the same direction. After how much time will they meet again at the starting point?
options: Time taken by slower runner for \(4\) laps
Time taken by faster runner for \(3\) laps
Time taken by slower runner for \(3\) laps
Time taken by faster runner for \(4\) laps
questions.keySolution:
Let speeds be \(3x\) and \(4x\)
Time for one lap: slower = \(600/3x = 200/x\), faster = \(600/4x = 150/x\)
LCM of \(200/x\) and \(150/x\) = \(600/x\)
This equals \(4 \times (200/x)\) = time for \(4\) laps by slower runner

questions.stem: In a circular race of \(400\) m, A gives B a start of \(40\) m and still beats him by \(20\) m. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.keySolution:
When A finishes \(400\) m, B covers \(400 - 20 = 380\) m from his starting point
B had \(40\) m head start, so B covered \(380 - 40 = 340\) m while A covered \(400\) m
Ratio of speeds A:B = \(400:340 = 20:17\)

questions.stem: Two cyclists start from diametrically opposite points of a circular track of \(800\) m and move in the same direction at \(8\) m/s and \(12\) m/s. When will they meet for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Initial distance between them = \(800/2 = 400\) m
Relative speed = \(12 - 8 = 4\) m/s
Time to meet = \(400/4 = 100\) seconds

questions.stem: A runs \(5/4\) times as fast as B. In a circular race, if A gives B a start of \(300\) m, A wins by \(60\) m. Find the length of the track.
questions.keySolution:
Let B's speed = \(4x\), A's speed = \(5x\)
Let track length = \(L\)
When A finishes \(L\), B covers \(L - 300 - 60 = L - 360\) m from his start
Time taken = \(L/5x\)
Distance by B in this time = \(4x \times L/5x = 4L/5\)
So \(4L/5 = L - 360\)
\(4L = 5L - 1800\)
\(L = 1800\) m

questions.stem: On a \(1000\) m circular track, A and B start at the same time from the same point in opposite directions at \(15\) m/s and \(10\) m/s. How many times will they meet in \(5\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(15 + 10 = 25\) m/s
Time for one meeting = \(1000/25 = 40\) seconds
In \(5\) minutes = \(300\) seconds
Number of meetings = \(300/40 = 7.5\) times

questions.stem: Three runners A, B, C start simultaneously from the same point on a \(600\) m circular track at speeds \(6\) m/s, \(8\) m/s, and \(12\) m/s in the same direction. After how much time will all three meet at the starting point?
questions.keySolution:
Time for A to complete one lap = \(600/6 = 100\) seconds
Time for B to complete one lap = \(600/8 = 75\) seconds  
Time for C to complete one lap = \(600/12 = 50\) seconds
LCM of \(100\), \(75\), and \(50\) = \(300\) seconds

questions.stem: Two trains run on a circular track of \(2000\) m in the same direction. Train A completes the track in \(100\) seconds and Train B in \(150\) seconds. Starting together, after how much time will A lap B for the third time?
questions.keySolution:
Speed of A = \(2000/100 = 20\) m/s
Speed of B = \(2000/150 = 40/3\) m/s
Relative speed = \(20 - 40/3 = 20/3\) m/s
Time for A to lap B once = \(2000/(20/3) = 300\) seconds
For third lapping = \(3 \times 300 = 900\) seconds

questions.stem: In a circular race of \(500\) m, A beats B by \(100\) m and C by \(150\) m. By how much distance will B beat C in the same race?
questions.keySolution:
When A covers \(500\) m, B covers \(400\) m, C covers \(350\) m
Speed ratio A:B:C = \(500:400:350 = 10:8:7\)
When B covers \(500\) m (completes race), C covers \(500 \times 7/8 = 437.5\) m
B beats C by \(500 - 437.5 = 62.5\) m

questions.stem: A circular track has a circumference of \(400\) m. Two athletes start from the same point and run in opposite directions at \(8\) m/s and \(6\) m/s. At what points on the track will they meet?
options: At \(228.57\) m and \(171.43\) m from start
questions.keySolution:
They meet every \(400/14 ≈ 28.57\) seconds
In \(28.57\) seconds, first athlete covers \(8 \times 28.57 = 228.57\) m
Second athlete covers \(6 \times 28.57 = 171.43\) m in opposite direction
They meet at these distances from starting point

questions.stem: On a \(300\) m circular track, X runs at \(9\) m/s and Y runs at \(6\) m/s in the same direction. If X gives Y a head start of \(60\) m, after how much time will X catch Y?
questions.keySolution:
Initial gap = \(60\) m
Relative speed = \(9 - 6 = 3\) m/s
Time to catch up = \(60/3 = 20\) seconds

questions.stem: Two motorcycles travel around a circular track of \(800\) m. The faster one completes \(5\) laps while the slower completes \(3\) laps in the same time when moving in the same direction. If they start together, when do they meet for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Speed ratio = \(5:3\)
They meet when faster covers one more lap than slower
Let slower cover \(x\) laps, faster covers \(5x/3\) laps
\(5x/3 - x = 1\)
\(2x/3 = 1\), so \(x = 1.5\)
Faster completes \(5 \times 1.5/3 = 2.5\) laps

questions.stem: A \(600\) m circular track has two runners starting from the same point. Runner A takes \(2\) minutes for one lap and Runner B takes \(3\) minutes. Running in the same direction, how many times will A overtake B in \(30\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
A completes one lap in \(2\) minutes, B in \(3\) minutes
Relative speed: A gains one lap every LCM(2,3) = 6 minutes
In \(30\) minutes, A overtakes B = \(30/6 = 5\) times

questions.stem: In a circular race, A runs at \(12\) km/h and B at \(8\) km/h. The track is \(400\) m long. If they start together in the same direction, what is the distance between them after \(3\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
A's speed = \(12 \times 5/18 = 10/3\) m/s
B's speed = \(8 \times 5/18 = 20/9\) m/s
In \(180\) seconds: A covers \(10/3 \times 180 = 600\) m
B covers \(20/9 \times 180 = 400\) m
Distance between them = \(600 - 400 = 200\) m

questions.stem: Two cars start from diametrically opposite points on a circular track of \(1000\) m and move towards each other at \(20\) m/s and \(30\) m/s. Where will they meet for the first time?
options: At the center of the track
questions.keySolution:
Total distance to cover = \(500\) m (half track)
Relative speed = \(20 + 30 = 50\) m/s
Time to meet = \(500/50 = 10\) seconds
Distance covered by first car = \(20 \times 10 = 200\) m from start

questions.stem: A and B are running on a circular track of \(800\) m in the same direction. A is running at \(18\) km/h and B at \(14\) km/h. They meet every:
questions.keySolution:
A's speed = \(18 \times 5/18 = 5\) m/s
B's speed = \(14 \times 5/18 = 35/9\) m/s
Relative speed = \(5 - 35/9 = 10/9\) m/s
Time to meet = \(800/(10/9) = 720\) seconds = \(12\) minutes

questions.stem: On a \(1200\) m circular track, runner P completes \(3\) laps in the time runner Q completes \(2\) laps. If they start together in the same direction, P will lap Q after how much distance covered by P?
questions.keySolution:
Speed ratio P:Q = \(3:2\)
When P laps Q, P covers one more complete lap than Q
Let Q cover distance \(d\), then P covers \(1.5d\)
For lapping: \(1.5d - d = 1200\)
\(0.5d = 1200\), so \(d = 2400\) m
Distance by P = \(1.5 \times 2400 = 3600\) m

questions.stem: Two horses race around a circular track. Horse A completes the track in \(80\) seconds, Horse B in \(100\) seconds. Starting together, how long before A gains a full lap on B?
questions.keySolution:
Speed of A = \(L/80\) where L is track length
Speed of B = \(L/100\)
Relative speed = \(L/80 - L/100 = L(100-80)/(80×100) = 20L/8000 = L/400\)
Time to gain one lap = \(L/(L/400) = 400\) seconds

questions.stem: In a circular race of \(500\) m, A gives B a start of \(50\) m. If A runs at \(10\) m/s and B at \(8\) m/s, by what distance does A win?
questions.keySolution:
Time for A to finish = \(500/10 = 50\) seconds
In \(50\) seconds, B covers = \(8 \times 50 = 400\) m from his starting position
B's total distance from original start = \(400 + 50 = 450\) m
A wins by \(500 - 450 = 50\) m
But B still needs \(500 - 450 = 50\) m more to finish
So A wins by \(50 + 50 = 100\) m

questions.stem: On a \(400\) m track, two runners start at the same time from the same point in opposite directions. They meet for the first time after \(40\) seconds. If one runs at \(6\) m/s, what is the speed of the other?
questions.keySolution:
Combined speed = Track length / Time to meet
Combined speed = \(400/40 = 10\) m/s
Speed of second runner = \(10 - 6 = 4\) m/s

questions.stem: Three cyclists A, B, and C race on a circular track of \(600\) m. A completes a lap in \(60\) s, B in \(80\) s, and C in \(120\) s. Starting together, after how much time will A and B meet at the starting point (excluding the start)?
questions.keySolution:
A completes lap in \(60\) s, B in \(80\) s
They meet at starting point after LCM of \(60\) and \(80\)
LCM(\(60, 80\)) = \(240\) seconds

questions.stem: Two athletes run around a \(400\) m track. The faster one runs at \(8\) m/s and laps the slower one every \(4\) minutes. What is the speed of the slower athlete?

In a circular race, when A runs \(400\) m, B runs \(350\) m and C runs \(300\) m in the same time. In a \(1000\) m race, if A gives B a start of \(60\) m and C a start of \(100\) m, who wins and by what margin?
options: A wins by \(25\) m over B
B wins by \(10\) m over A
A wins by \(15\) m over B
A wins by \(65\) m over B
questions.keySolution:
Speed ratio A:B:C = \(400:350:300 = 8:7:6\)
When A finishes \(1000\) m, B covers \(1000 \times 7/8 = 875\) m from his starting point
B's total position = \(875 + 60 = 935\) m from original start line
A wins by \(1000 - 935 = 65\) m over B

questions.stem: A \(1000\) m circular track has two points A and B diametrically opposite. Two runners start simultaneously from A and B and run in the same direction. They first meet at a point \(200\) m from A. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.keySolution:
Let runner from A be faster
When they meet: Runner from A covers \(200\) m
Runner from B covers \(500 - 300 = 200\) m to reduce the gap and reach meeting point
But runner from B actually covers \(500 + 200 = 700\) m total distance
Speed ratio = \(200:(1000-200) = 200:800 = 1:4\) is wrong
Correct approach: In first meeting, together they cover track length
Runner A covers \(200\) m, Runner B covers \(1000 - 200 = 800\) m
Speed ratio = \(200:800 = 1:4\)

Runner A covers \(200\) m, Runner B covers \(500 + 200 = 700\) m
Ratio = \(200:700 = 2:7\)

If they meet at distance \(d\) from faster runner's start, ratio = \(d:(L-d)\) where L is initial separation
Here L = 500m (half track), d = 200m
But they meet at 200m from A means A is faster
Speed ratio = \(500+200:500-200 = 700:300 = 7:3\)

questions.stem: Two sprinters race on a \(200\) m circular track in opposite directions at \(8\) m/s and \(12\) m/s. How far from the starting point do they meet for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Combined speed = \(8 + 12 = 20\) m/s
Time to meet = \(200/20 = 10\) seconds
Distance covered by first sprinter = \(8 \times 10 = 80\) m from start

questions.stem: On a circular track of \(500\) m, A and B start together in the same direction. A runs at \(5\) m/s and B at \(4\) m/s. How many complete laps will A have completed when he first laps B?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(5 - 4 = 1\) m/s
Time to lap B = \(500/1 = 500\) seconds
Distance covered by A in \(500\) seconds = \(5 \times 500 = 2500\) m
Number of laps = \(2500/500 = 5\) laps

questions.stem: A circular race track is \(800\) m long. If two cars start from the same point in opposite directions at \(60\) km/h and \(40\) km/h, after how many seconds will they meet for the second time?
questions.keySolution:
Speed of car 1 = \(60 \times 5/18 = 50/3\) m/s
Speed of car 2 = \(40 \times 5/18 = 100/9\) m/s
Combined speed = \(50/3 + 100/9 = 150/9 + 100/9 = 250/9\) m/s
Time for first meeting = \(800/(250/9) = 800 \times 9/250 = 28.8\) seconds
Time for second meeting = \(2 \times 28.8 = 57.6\) seconds

questions.stem: In a \(600\) m circular race, A gives B a start of \(100\) m and beats him by \(50\) m. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.keySolution:
When A completes \(600\) m, B covers \(600 - 50 = 550\) m from his starting point
B had \(100\) m head start, so effectively B ran \(550 - 100 = 450\) m while A ran \(600\) m
Speed ratio A:B = \(600:450 = 4:3\)

questions.stem: Two motorcyclists start from the same point on a circular track of \(400\) m and travel in the same direction at \(72\) km/h and \(54\) km/h. When will the faster one be exactly halfway around the track ahead of the slower one?
questions.keySolution:
Speed of faster = \(72 \times 5/18 = 20\) m/s
Speed of slower = \(54 \times 5/18 = 15\) m/s
Relative speed = \(20 - 15 = 5\) m/s
For faster to be \(200\) m (halfway) ahead: Time = \(200/5 = 40\) seconds

questions.stem: A \(800\) m track has three runners A, B, C with speeds \(8\) m/s, \(6\) m/s, \(4\) m/s respectively, all starting together in the same direction. When will all three be together again at the starting point?
questions.keySolution:
Time for A to complete one lap = \(800/8 = 100\) seconds
Time for B to complete one lap = \(800/6 = 400/3\) seconds
Time for C to complete one lap = \(800/4 = 200\) seconds
LCM of \(100\), \(400/3\), and \(200\) = \(400\) seconds

questions.stem: Two athletes are running around a circular track in opposite directions. They meet every \(48\) seconds. If they run in the same direction, the faster one overtakes the other every \(240\) seconds. Find the ratio of their speeds.

On a \(500\) m circular track, runner A takes \(100\) seconds to complete one lap. Runner B takes \(125\) seconds. If they start together in the same direction, how far apart will they be after \(10\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
Speed of A = \(500/100 = 5\) m/s
Speed of B = \(500/125 = 4\) m/s
In \(600\) seconds (\(10\) minutes):
A covers \(5 \times 600 = 3000\) m = \(6\) complete laps (position 0)
B covers \(4 \times 600 = 2400\) m = \(4.8\) laps = \(4\) complete + \(400\) m
B is at position \(400\) m from start
Distance apart = minimum of \(400\) m or \(500-400 = 100\) m = \(100\) m

questions.stem: In a circular race of \(1000\) m, three friends A, B, C start together. A beats B by \(50\) m and C by \(100\) m. If B and C race the same distance, by how much will B beat C?
questions.keySolution:
When A covers \(1000\) m, B covers \(950\) m, C covers \(900\) m
Speed ratio A:B:C = \(1000:950:900 = 20:19:18\)
When B covers \(1000\) m, C covers \(1000 \times 18/19 = 947.37\) m
B beats C by \(1000 - 947.37 = 52.63\) m

questions.stem: Two cars race on a circular track of \(600\) m. Car X completes \(5\) laps in the time car Y completes \(4\) laps. If they start together, after how much time will X lap Y for the first time?
options: Time for Y to complete \(4\) laps
Time for Y to complete \(5\) laps
Time for X to complete \(4\) laps
Time for X to complete \(5\) laps
questions.keySolution:
Speed ratio X:Y = \(5:4\)
X laps Y when X completes one more lap than Y
Let Y complete \(n\) laps, then X completes \(5n/4\) laps
For lapping: \(5n/4 - n = 1\)
\(n/4 = 1\), so \(n = 4\) laps
Time = Time for Y to complete \(4\) laps

questions.stem: A \(400\) m circular track has two runners starting from diametrically opposite points and running towards each other at \(6\) m/s and \(4\) m/s. After they meet, they continue in their original directions. When will they meet for the second time?
questions.keySolution:
First meeting: They cover half track = \(200\) m combined
Time = \(200/(6+4) = 20\) seconds
After first meeting, for second meeting they need to cover full track = \(400\) m
Time = \(400/10 = 40\) seconds
Total time from start = \(20 + 40 = 60\) seconds

questions.stem: On a \(800\) m track, A runs at \(16\) m/s and B at \(12\) m/s in the same direction starting together. What is the minimum number of complete laps A must run to lap B twice?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(16 - 12 = 4\) m/s
Time to lap B once = \(800/4 = 200\) seconds
Time to lap B twice = \(2 \times 200 = 400\) seconds
Distance covered by A in \(400\) seconds = \(16 \times 400 = 6400\) m
Number of complete laps = \(6400/800 = 8\) laps

questions.stem: Two joggers run around a circular park of \(300\) m in opposite directions at \(5\) m/s and \(7\) m/s starting from the same point. How many times will they cross each other in \(5\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(5 + 7 = 12\) m/s
Time for one crossing = \(300/12 = 25\) seconds
In \(5\) minutes = \(300\) seconds
Number of crossings = \(300/25 = 12\) times

questions.stem: A \(1200\) m circular track has three runners A, B, C with speeds in ratio \(6:5:4\). They start together in the same direction. After what time will B be exactly between A and C for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Let speeds be \(6v, 5v, 4v\) for A, B, C respectively
For B to be exactly between A and C:
A gains on C at rate \((6v-4v) = 2v\)
Time for A to gain half lap (\(600\) m) on C = \(600/2v = 300/v\)
At this time, A is \(600\) m ahead of C, and B is \(300\) m ahead of C
So B is exactly between A and C
For \(v = 1\) m/s: Time = \(300\) seconds
For \(v = 0.5\) m/s: Time = \(600\) seconds
Given the answer is \(600\) seconds, \(v = 0.5\) m/s

questions.stem: Two friends A and B decide to race on a circular track of \(400\) m. A gives B a head start and waits for \(20\) seconds before starting. If A runs at \(8\) m/s and B at \(6\) m/s, when will A catch up to B?
questions.keySolution:
In \(20\) seconds, B covers \(6 \times 20 = 120\) m head start
Let A catch B after time \(t\) from when A starts
Distance by A in time \(t\) = \(8t\)
Distance by B in time \(t\) = \(6t + 120\) (including head start)
When A catches B: \(8t = 6t + 120\)
\(2t = 120\)
\(t = 60\) seconds

questions.stem: On a \(500\) m circular track, runner P takes \(50\) seconds per lap and runner Q takes \(75\) seconds per lap. Starting together in the same direction, what is the distance between them after \(150\) seconds?
questions.keySolution:
In \(150\) seconds:
P completes \(150/50 = 3\) laps exactly
Q completes \(150/75 = 2\) laps exactly
Since both complete whole numbers of laps, they meet at the starting point
Distance between them = \(0\) m

questions.stem: In a circular race of \(800\) m, A can run \(2\) m/s faster than B. If A gives B a \(160\) m head start and still wins by \(40\) m, find B's speed.
questions.keySolution:
Let B's speed = \(v\) m/s, A's speed = \((v+2)\) m/s
Time for A to finish \(800\) m = \(800/(v+2)\)
In this time, B covers = \(v \times 800/(v+2)\) m from his starting point
B's position from original start = \(v \times 800/(v+2) + 160\)
A wins by \(40\) m means: \(800 - [v \times 800/(v+2) + 160] = 40\)
\(640 = v \times 800/(v+2)\)
\(640(v+2) = 800v\)
\(640v + 1280 = 800v\)
\(160v = 1280\)
\(v = 8\) m/s
